requirements.source: F5 iRules after: the script word's position depends on whether -periodic and a millisecond count precede it
F5 iRules clientside: the script is evaluated immediately, in the clientside flow context
F5 iRules proc: the body is stored on the iRule and run per call
F5 iRules when: the event handler's body position depends on the event and priority words
SDC base `foreach_in_collection var collection body`: the pack declares `arg 2 -role Body` (specs/sdc_base.tclspec l.228-234)
requirements.notes: A loop body rather than a callback, and same-invocation for that reason — kept in the manifest because it is the shape a vendor pack most easily loses.

requirements.source: SpecTcl pack DSL (docs/design/spec-packs.md): a `command` declaration's brace body is evaluated as pack declarations

IEEE UPF create_upf_library -contents: the option value is a UPF/Tcl body evaluated in the library's protected namespace; the pack declares it `option -contents -takes upf_commands -role Body` (specs/upf.tclspec l.735-739)
IEEE UPF define_power_model: the body is the last word of whichever option set the call carries, so the pack resolves the role per call (`arg_role_resolver` at specs/upf.tclspec l.815-825)
requirements.notes: A pack-declared resolver must stay a `dynamic` row for the same reason a native one does.

requirements.source: Xilinx Vivado add_condition: the trailing `commands` word is Tcl run when the condition is met; the pack declares it `arg 1 -role Body -layout BlockScript` (specs/eda_xilinx.tclspec l.83-89)
requirements.notes: The EDA vendor libraries are bundled SpecTcl loadables, so this row exists only because the projection walks the pack-installed stores as well as the native ones.

requirements.source: Expect exit(1): -onexit installs a handler run at exit; nothing is documented as appended, so the contract stays unknown
Expect trap(1): the action is a script evaluated when the trapped signal arrives
Tcl after(n) cancel: the first value is either an opaque timer id or the exact script text of a pending handler
requirements.notes: Catalogue-seeded union: classifying every word as Tcl code would invent references for timer ids.

requirements.source: Tcl apply(n): the lambda term is applied during this invocation
Tcl chan(n) copy: "identical to fcopy" — the callback takes the count, plus an error message when the copy failed
requirements.notes: The other half of the #1706 parity control; `chan` itself is 8.5+, so the floor differs from `fcopy` while the contract does not.

requirements.source: Tcl refchan(n): the handler synopsis is `cmdPrefix subcommand channel ?args?` for every method (`cmdPrefix cgetall channel` is the shortest), so at least the subcommand and the channel are appended

imprecision.reason: positional command prefixes carry no per-slot timing axis, so the row reports the command-wide DEFERS_BODY answer; the prefix is in fact stored and invoked later

requirements.notes: Reflected-channel handler: the prefix is stored on the channel and invoked for every operation on it.

requirements.source: Tcl chan(n) event: "arranges for the Tcl script script to be called whenever the channel ... becomes readable or writable"; chan.n defers to fileevent(n) for the semantics
requirements.oracle: tclsh8.5/8.6/9.0/9.1, `proc p {ch} { chan event $ch readable {error stop}; set ::reached 1 }`: ::reached is set, so the script is stored, not run
requirements.notes: The registered script runs from the event loop at global level, exactly as `fileevent`'s does.

requirements.source: Tcl transchan(n): the handler synopsis is `cmdPrefix subcommand handle ?args?` for every method (`cmdPrefix clear handle` is the shortest)

imprecision.reason: positional command prefixes carry no per-slot timing axis, so the row reports the command-wide DEFERS_BODY answer; the prefix is in fact stored and invoked later

requirements.notes: Version-gated control: `chan push` arrived in 8.6, so this row must not reach 8.4/8.5 even though `chan` itself is 8.5+.

requirements.source: Tcl coroutine(n) coroinject: "An additional two arguments are appended ... The first is the name of the command that suspended the coroutine (yield or yieldto), and the second is the argument ... that is the current resumption value" (coroutine.n l.106-110)
Tcl coroutine(n) coroprobe: the prefix is run inside the coroutine's frame with nothing documented as appended, so the contract stays unknown

Tcl coroutine(n): `coroutine name command ?arg...?` calls the command prefix with "the other remaining arguments" and nothing of its own, so no appended count is documented and the contract stays unknown

imprecision.reason: positional command prefixes carry no per-slot timing axis, so the row reports the command-wide DEFERS_BODY answer; the prefix is in fact stored and invoked later

requirements.source: Tcl fcopy(n): "callback ... is called with the number of bytes written ... If an error occurred ... the error string is passed as a second argument"
requirements.oracle: tclsh8.4/8.6: `fcopy $in $out -command cb` calls `cb 206`; copying /dev/zero to /dev/full on 8.6 calls `cb 0 {error writing "file4": no space left on device}`
requirements.notes: Parity control for issue #1706: this row and `chan copy -command` must stay identical in kind, timing, and appended arity.

requirements.source: Tcl fileevent(n): "The script for a file event is executed at global level (outside the context of any Tcl procedure)"
requirements.oracle: tclsh8.6.16/9.0.4, `proc p {} { fileevent $ch readable {error stop}; set ::reached 1 }`: ::reached is set (issue #1672 audit)
requirements.notes: `chan event`'s legacy spelling; the two rows must agree.

requirements.source: Tcl http(n) -command: "invoked ... after the HTTP transaction completes" with the token appended

Tcl interp(n) limit: the callback script is evaluated when the limit is exceeded, in the interpreter that set it
Tcl lsort(n) -command: "evaluate a Tcl script consisting of command with the two elements appended as additional arguments" (lsort.n l.62-64)

Tcl namespace(n) ensemble: the unknown handler is called with the ensemble command and the unresolved subcommand words; the argument count depends on the call being dispatched, so the contract is deliberately unknown
requirements.notes: Conservative-by-design control: `unknown` appended arity must stay `unknown` rather than being guessed.

requirements.source: Tcl namespace(n) unknown: "the full invocation line will be appended to the handler" (namespace.n l.326)

imprecision.reason: positional command prefixes carry no per-slot timing axis, so the row reports the command-wide DEFERS_BODY answer; the prefix is in fact stored and invoked later

requirements.source: Tcl package(n) ifneeded: the script is stored and evaluated later, when the package is required
Tcl package(n) unknown: "Tcl appends one or more additional arguments giving the desired package name and requirements" (package.n l.176-178)
requirements.oracle: tclsh8.4/8.6/9.0/9.1, `package unknown handler; package require nosuchpkg`: the handler is called with two words — `nosuchpkg {}` on 8.4 and `nosuchpkg 0-` on 8.6/9.0/9.1 — so the synthesised requirement keeps the appended count at 2 even though package.n's prose says "only the name will be added"

requirements.source: Tcl proc(n): the body is stored and evaluated when the procedure is invoked
Tcl regsub(n) -command (9.0+): the replacement word is a command prefix only under -command, so the role is resolver-decided

Tcl socket(n): the command prefix is invoked with "three additional arguments: the name of the new channel, the address, in network address notation, of the client's host, and the client's port number" (socket.n l.124)
Tcl tcltest(n) customMatch: the script is called with the expected and actual results appended
Tcl trace(n) add: the appended-argument contract depends on the trace type and ops words, so the position and arity are resolver-decided
requirements.notes: Dynamic-by-design control: a resolver must stay an explicit `dynamic` row rather than being flattened into a guessed static position.

requirements.appended_arity: type/ops-dependent: exactly 2, exactly 3, exactly 4, or one of [2, 4]
requirements.source: Tcl trace(n) remove: the prefix identifies a registration to delete; it is navigable executable text but is neither invoked nor stored
requirements.notes: Catalogue-seeded row: the registry shape cannot express "named but never run", so the classification is audited seed data.

requirements.source: Tcl 8.6 trace(n) vdelete: the legacy variable-trace removal form, retired in Tcl 9.0
requirements.notes: Version-gated control in the other direction: this row must not reach 9.0/9.1.

tcllib snit(n): the method body is stored on the type and run per call
tcllib struct::graph(n) walk: the command is called with the graph, the direction, and the node
tcllib struct::list(n) split: the predicate is called with one element
tcllib struct::tree(n) walkproc: the prefix's position depends on the option words that precede it
tcllib uevent(n) bind: the prefix is called with the tag, event, and the event's detail dictionary

Tk button(n) -command: "specifies a Tcl command to associate with the button ... invoked when mouse button 1 is released"
Tk options(n) -xscrollcommand: "the widget will generate a Tcl command by concatenating the scroll command and two numbers" (options.n l.330-338)
Tk entry(n) -validatecommand: evaluated when the widget's validation triggers fire, with the percent substitutions applied
Tk menu(n) -tearoffcommand: "the value of this option, followed by ... the name of the menu window, followed by ... the name of the torn off menu window" (menu.n l.46-51)

requirements.source: Tk selection(n) handle: the retrieval command's position depends on the option words that precede it
Tk text(n) dump -command: called for each element with the key, value and index appended, during the dump itself
Tk text(n) sync: the command is run once the widget's line metrics are up to date, with nothing appended
Tk tk_messageBox(n) -command: invoked when the dialog closes; the appended arguments are platform-dependent and stay unknown
Tk ttk_treeview(n) sort: the comparison prefix is called with two item values during the sort
Tk wm(n) protocol: the handler word is present only in the setting form

known_gaps.source: Tcl http(n) -proxyfilter: the filter command decides whether a request goes through a proxy
known_gaps.notes: Called as `$http(-proxyfilter) $host` — one appended argument — in library/http/http.tcl (8.6.16 l.944; 9.0.4 l.1299 and l.4967). The registry's http::config spec carries no OptionSpec table at all, so none of its six options has a value descriptor to classify; giving it one is the work this waiver tracks.

known_gaps.source: Tcl http(n) register: `http::register proto port command` stores the prefix http::geturl opens sockets with
known_gaps.notes: library/http/http.tcl builds the call as `[list {*}$defcmd {*}$sockopts {*}$targs {*}$targetAddr]` (9.0.4 l.1407; 8.6.16 l.1112/1140), so host and port are always appended — at least 2. Classifying it makes the registered head a resolved command reference, and the head real code passes is `::tls::socket` from a package the registry does not model, so W123's unknown-command answer has to be settled before the declaration lands.

The websocket package is registered from a flat name/arity/synopsis table (tcl-registry/src/commands/tcllib/ensembles.rs) with no argument roles, so the handler word has no descriptor to carry a classification. Restructuring that table is what closes this.

known_gaps.source: tcllib ftp(n): -progress, -output and -command install transfer callbacks on the session
known_gaps.notes: `ftp::Open` is registered from the same flat table and declares no options at all, so its three documented callbacks have nowhere to live yet.

known_gaps.source: Xilinx Vivado create_qor_check -rule_body: names the Tcl procedure the check runs (specs/eda_xilinx.tclspec l.3291)
known_gaps.notes: Declared `-takes rule_body` — a plain value — in the bundled pack. The sibling `create_drc_check -rule_body` and `create_gui_custom_command -command` are the same shape. No Vivado is installable here, so the prefix-versus-script union stays unverified rather than guessed; the projection does walk the pack-installed stores, so classifying one in the pack closes this waiver.
